question: Can the public X16 command and AVI archives support an identity-indexed missing-frame ledger, or only an aggregate trigger-frame count comparison?

causalChain.inputAndAllowedAssumptions: Official ZIP central directories, complete CRC-verified XYPT members, nested 4 MiB and 8 MiB AVI archive prefixes, and documented four-column trigger semantics.
causalChain.bottleneck: The AVI header exposes aggregate frame totals but no public frame-to-trigger identity key.
causalChain.bridgeClaim: Agreement among avih.dwTotalFrames, video strh.dwLength, and dmlh.dwTotalFrames makes the aggregate count reproducible.
causalChain.independentAdjudicand: A separate Python ZIP64, CSV, and AVI parser reproduces counts, source hashes, retained-prefix hashes, and native counters.
causalChain.resolutionBoundary: Aggregate deficits are established; missing-frame identities, causes, and tail placement are not.

uncertaintyAndIndependence.sampling: Two layers only; L0001 was development and L0002 was a frozen holdout.
uncertaintyAndIndependence.measurement: Counts come from digital trigger masks and three agreeing AVI header counters, not decoded image content.
uncertaintyAndIndependence.model: A count difference does not identify which trigger lacked a frame or why.
uncertaintyAndIndependence.implementation: JavaScript and Python parsers are independent, but both use the installed 7-Zip 22.01 Deflate64 decoder.
uncertaintyAndIndependence.extrapolation: No loss-rate claim is extrapolated to the remaining 248 layers or other builds.

nextDecisiveTest: Preregister a development/holdout dynamic sequence-alignment protocol that compares XY command motion and image-derived melt-pool trajectories, inserts synthetic deletions as positive controls, and requires a separate implementation to recover held-out deletion identities before interpreting natural discrepancies.
